Exact diagonal coordinate projection yields independent geometric survival factors for each coordinate; maximizing a diagonal weighted quadratic form yields the sharp rate for every t>=1. Sorted-index comparison proves the consecutive-window global optimum and strict window necessity for distinct weights. Finite inclusion-exclusion and summation establish exact completion-time distribution/expectation. All four rational candidates and the three-row divergent surrogate ratio were reconstructed. The extracted checker passed 15,133 exact-rational assertions, supplementary to the general proof. The result explicitly counts zero-update iid draws, avoiding confusion with rejection-resampling implementations.

originality.rationale: PASS with priority risk. Original 2026 source Section 3.2 supplies a general rate proxy and Frobenius row-ID selector, but not an exact all-budget diagonal pin-set classification or a rate-vs-completion objective conflict. The earlier SCRK source supplies the update and rate estimate; classical randomized Kaczmarz/coupon formulas are explicitly prior knowledge. value.rationale: PASS. Fixed-row selection is a current algorithm-design question, and sharp worst-case mean-square error plus exact finite completion are two motivated, genuinely distinct objectives. The consecutive-window theorem solves an entire exact diagonal model, the exact four-row table demonstrates a nontrivial objective conflict, and the three-row family quantifies a structurally unbounded Frobenius-surrogate gap. It does not claim wall-clock, noisy-data or Sun-algorithm accepted-step disadvantages; zero-residual conditional rejection removes the diagonal waiting-time effect.
